## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`save_report` must stop reporting success when the write fails, because the swallowed `OSError` tells users a report was saved when it was not; the save-failure test needs to be strengthened alongside that fix.

## Changes
Adds `save_report` to write the rendered report to a path and print its destination, and `cleanup_report` to delete a temporary report while tolerating an absent file. It also adds tests for both functions.

## Critical
- app/reports.py:8 — silent-failure — Propagate or signal write failures in save_report — When `path.write_text` raises `OSError` (missing parent directory, permission denied, full disk), `except OSError: pass` discards it. Line 10 then prints "Report saved to {path}" and line 11 returns 0. — Users and calling scripts are told the report was saved, see exit status 0, and lose the report without any error. — Fix: Remove the `try`/`except` or re-raise, or return a non-zero status with an actionable message, so the success print runs only after a successful write.

## Important
- tests/test_reports.py:14 — tests — Assert the failure outcome in the unavailable-destination test — `test_save_with_unavailable_destination` calls `save_report` on a path whose parent is missing and asserts nothing, so it passes while the function falsely prints success and returns 0. — The only test for the save-failure path gives no regression protection and currently accepts the silent-success behavior.
